newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - March 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - March 20.

text.p: MLADA FRONTA DNES - The cabinet rejected Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy's proposal for resolving the situation at the Poldi steelworks. Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said the material was not concrete, and Dlouhy has until the middle of April to work further on the material.
- German RWE Energie, a leading producer of electricity, obtained a 10.33 percent stake in Stredoceska Energeticka.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Disputes between the management of Czech Railways and the railway workers' union over wage increases this year continue, even after yesterday's negotiations.

- Severoceska Energetika was paid the 23 million crowns owed it by Czech Railways for electricity. The energy company had warned that if the debt was not paid by yesterday, it would cut off electricity for tracks in parts of the north.
- The advertising market began this year with a slight decrease in prices. Experts say it's a seasonal trend.

- During the first months of this year, there was a fall in retail sales. While in January of 1996, there was an increase of 9.4 percent, there was a fall this year of 2.3 percent, according to the Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU).
PRAVO - President Vaclav Havel will travel to Bonn soon to speak before the German parliament. German President Roman Herzog should also travel to Prague to speak to the Czech parliament.
- Yugoslav automotive corporation Zastava will place its passenger car Yugo back on the Czech market and will also offer its utility vehicles Iveco Zastava.

- Skoda Plzen signed a contract yesterday for the supply of energy equipment to the Norwegian company Norsk Hydro and also for the supply of equipment for petrochemical operations for Norwegian companies.
LIDOVE NOVINY - The Senate approved a law to change the Czech border with Slovakia, which is the first constitutional law that the Senate has ever addressed.
- According to Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus, the Motol hospital will continue to provide for its patients, even though it is threatened with bankruptcy.
- Yesterday, the cabinet approved material presented by the Finance Ministry for a law for taxes on realty and for administration of taxes and payments.
